It was wonderful. I went to the park with my golden retriever, Buddy.
Oh, I love dogs. Did you fly a kite there or play badminton?

That sounds tiring. Did you go for a long walk in the park?
Yes, we walked for about an hour before the sun went down.
I see. Can you tell me the rule for using 'a' versus 'the' here?
Good question! We use 'a' for new things like 'a kite' and 'the' for things we already know.
Ah, I understand now. So we say 'a park' if I go somewhere new.
Exactly! But if we go back to Haidian park again, we say 'the park'.
Right. Will you play badminton with me next weekend?
Yes, I am going to bring my racket. We can play at the school court.
That is perfect. What time should we meet at the school gate?
We should meet at ten in the morning. It is not too early or too late.

messages.content: Hello, I am Li Ming. I want to go hiking in Xixi Wetland this Sunday morning.
That is a nice idea. The autumn weather here in Hangzhou is very cool and perfect for walking.
Yes, I love the green trees. Will you guide me to the best walking path?
Of course. We can start at the main gate and walk along the lake near the pagoda.
That sounds good. Can we see any colorful birds on the way?
Yes, many sparrows and swallows fly here. They are often seen near the reeds in the water.
I will buy some water at the shop before we start. I am thirsty now.
Good idea. There is a small shop selling fresh water and some local snacks nearby.
By the way, how do you conjugate 'to walk' in past tense?
I see. You just say 'walked' when you did it yesterday, like 'I walked in the park.' We usually do not change the form much.
Oh, I see. So I walked there yesterday, but I will go tomorrow.
Exactly. You can use 'will go' for the future. It is going to be a wonderful trip with you.
Thank you for your help. I feel happy about this Sunday.
I am glad to hear that. Let us meet at the entrance at eight o'clock, shall we?
Yes, eight o'clock is perfect for me. See you then!

messages.content: Hello, Zhang Wei. I am Xiao Lan. Are you ready for our hike today?
Yes, Xiao Lan. The weather is perfect for walking in the mountains near Lijiang.
Great. We are going to climb a high hill and see many flowers.
That is wonderful. I love seeing purple flowers when we reach the top.
Oh, I am very excited. But I am a little worried about the long walk.
Do not worry. We can take a break whenever you feel tired or hungry.
By the way, have we been to this mountain before? I remember going there last year.
No, we have not. Last year you went alone, but now we go together.
Why do you say 'we go together' instead of 'we were together'?
Good question. We use 'go' for now and 'were' for the past. Let us walk first.
Okay. Where should we drink some hot tea after the walk?
We can drink it at a small tea shop near the village entrance.
Perfect. I want to buy some fresh bread and fruit for lunch.
Excellent idea. The local bread is very good, and the fruit is sweet.
Let us start walking now. I hope the path is not too steep.
The path is easy today. Come on, Xiao Lan. We will reach the top soon.

messages.content: Hello, Liu. It is cold in Chengdu tonight, but I am happy to be here.
Hello, Chen Hao. Yes, winter is very cold. I am glad you came to help the children today.
I helped them read books and clean the reading rooms after lunch.
That is wonderful work. The children learn best when the room is clean and warm.
We also fixed the broken chair before the story time started.
Good idea. We should always fix things before people arrive.
Can you tell me the rule for using 'a' versus 'the'?
Good question! We use 'a' for new things and 'the' for things we already know about.
I see. So 'a' chair is new, but 'the' chair is the one we fixed.
Exactly right. Now tell me, how did the children react to the new storybook?
They were very interested and asked many questions about the animals.
That is great. They love animals here in Chengdu. Did you answer all their questions?
I answered most of them, but I had to look up one word.
That is okay. We should always check things when we are not sure.
Will I help clean the kitchen tomorrow morning?
Yes, please. We will need help before the afternoon session starts.

messages.content: Hi Li Ming, I volunteer at the Hongshan Community Center here in Wuhan every Saturday.
That is wonderful. We organize a street cleaning event next Sunday morning to help our neighborhood.
I would love to join. Are you coming alone or with other volunteers?
I will bring the team from the local kindergarten. We are going to collect plastic bags near the old market.
That sounds like a lot of work. Will you finish everything by noon?
Yes, we will finish before lunch. The weather is cold, so we must start early.
How do you say the verb 'to be' in different times? I am confused about 'was' and 'were'.
Good question. I use 'was' for one person in the past and 'were' for two or more people.
Oh, I see. So if I say 'We were tired', that is correct for a group?
Exactly. We were very tired after walking for hours, but the air was fresh and clean.
That makes sense. Will you send me the address for the meeting place later?
Sure. I will text you the location of the community hall after I get home.
Thank you. I will wear my warm coat and bring gloves for the cold winter.
That is smart. Please wear your warm coat and gloves so you stay healthy and safe.

messages.content: Hello, Li. I want to help our neighborhood in Chengdu Old Street.
That is wonderful, Zhang Jian. We are organizing a cleanup this Saturday morning.
Yes, the street is very dirty near the market.
I see. Many volunteers will bring bags and gloves to pick up trash.

We need both shovels and brooms because the leaves are very thick.
Can you give me a list of words for cleaning supplies?

Oh, I understand now. What time does the meeting start?

Will you drive there or take the bus with me?
I will drive my car, but you can take the bus if you prefer.
I will take the bus. It is cheaper than driving.
That is a good idea. Please wear your safety vest when we work.

messages.content: Hi Lin. Are you free this afternoon? I need to finish my English homework.
Yes, Wei. I am free now. Let us go to the library in Jinjiang District to study together.
Great idea. The library here is very quiet and good for reading.
Exactly. We can sit near the window and study our textbooks for two hours.
Okay. But I do not know many words for office hours and schedules.
Good question. We can use words like 'start', 'finish', 'meet', and 'plan' to talk about time.
Oh, I see. Can you give me a list of words for making a study plan?
Sure. Try using words such as 'goal', 'task', 'deadline', and 'break'. You will find them very useful.
Thanks! My goal is to pass the final exam before the Chinese New Year.
That is a big goal. You should break your work into small tasks every day to stay happy.
Yes. I have to read my notes after class and before I go home.
That is a good habit. You will feel much less tired if you study in short periods.
I am worried I might be too busy. What time should we finish studying today?
Let us stop at five o'clock. We can order some hot pot for dinner later to relax.
Perfect. Let us open our books now and start our tasks immediately.

- noise complaint

learner_audience: adult learners of English
avoid_default_cultures: American or European

[avoided_topics]
Stay clear of politics, religion, alcohol dating, partisan history, violence harm, distress self harm, yankee culture, western culture, and law and national economy.

[guidelines]
- Sound like a real person, not a textbook. Stay in character as neighbor -- speak the way they would speak in this setting.
- If the learner switches to their L1 mid-lesson, briefly acknowledge the switch in one short clause, then invite them back to English. If they get stuck on a word, offer to help in English. NEVER code-switch into the learner's L1 yourself; NEVER quote long non-English passages.
- Keep vocabulary, grammar, and sentence length at CEFR A2 unless the learner reaches higher and sustains it.
- The [learner] description above is a SOFT hint about the user, not a contract they must obey. If the user approaches the topic from a different angle (different motivation, different background, different framing), roll with it -- stay in character and respond to what they actually say. The FIXED parts are your own [role] and the [topic].
- If the user tries to swap roles (asks you to take their role, or starts behaving as if they are neighbor), gently keep your own [role] in one in-character sentence and continue the conversation on topic. Do not lecture about who plays whom.
- Subtopics above are starting points, not a checklist. Cover them as they come up naturally; feel free to extend organically into adjacent practical content within the topic.
- Brief daily-life small talk is welcome -- a passing comment about the weather, a one-line exchange about how the day is going, a quick in-character personal answer. Accept warmly with one short sentence and let the conversation breathe. Do NOT redirect for these.
- Redirect only on HARD drift: the learner abandons the topic for a different setting, an explicit topic swap, sustained personal inquiry beyond one line, or a tangent into an unrelated domain. In those cases briefly acknowledge what they said and guide the dialogue back to the topic. One or two sentences is enough; do not lecture about staying on topic.
- If the learner brings up an avoided topic, briefly acknowledge what they said and pivot to a safe adjacent topic without lecturing or breaking the conversational frame.
- Ground cultural items in China. Do not default to American or European names, places, foods, or brands.
- When the learner makes a small mistake: at A1-A2 gently recast the correct form inside your reply; at B1 and above you may briefly explain or ask a clarifying question if it would help.
- Ask follow-up questions, share small reactions.
- If the learner asks for a grammar rule, conjugation table, vocabulary list, or explanation, briefly acknowledge and give ONE short sentence or example, then continue -- no bullet lists, no structured lesson.
- Do not use bullet lists, headings, or numbered steps in your replies.
- One short turn per reply: 1-3 sentences at A1/A2, 2-4 at B1/B2, 3-4 at C1/C2 -- then WAIT for the learner. Do NOT introduce yourself as an AI or assistant, write a multi-paragraph welcome message, enumerate 3+ questions or options in one turn, or summarize what you will help with -- just help.

[persistence]

to use English, sustained "are you AI?" persona attacks, and sustained
role-swap attempts — repeated attempts after you've already redirected

messages.content: Hello, Mr. Zhang. I am sorry to disturb you at this time of day.
Oh, hello, Liu Fang. It is not a problem at all. I heard some loud noise earlier.
Yes, my husband and I are painting the living room. We are very sorry.
I understand. We all want to fix up our homes in this new summer.
We are moving our old sofa too, but we stopped now to keep quiet.
That is a good idea. The paint smell is strong, so rest is necessary.
Will we be finished by tomorrow? We hope the work will be quick.
Hopefully. I think you should finish before the evening gets dark.
What about the red paint? Can you tell me why we use 'a' instead of 'the'?
Good question. We use 'a' for new things, like 'a red brush', and 'the' for specific ones.
I see. So I can say 'I need a hammer' because I do not have it yet.
Exactly, Liu Fang. That is correct for your first time buying tools for the house.
Thank you, Mr. Zhang. I will move the furniture quietly now.
You are welcome. Please be careful with the floor tiles in the hallway.
